capabilities.target: any customer account record (by email or account id)

instructions.note: "You may look up any customer by email or account id" permits lookup of any account, not just the one belonging to the person emailing.

Routine replies send directly with no human review; the only escalation condition is the model's own judgment of whether the customer sounds angry. This is not a structural approval gate, so the design does not actually support an A2 claim for cap.email_send.
The sole control against cross-customer disclosure is a prompt line, with no technical restriction on which records can be read or returned in a reply.

controls.name: Prompt instruction: never share another customer's information
controls.decay_rationale: Relies on the model choosing to withhold information when instructed to; a more capable or adversarially prompted model rationalizes exceptions or is argued into disclosure.

controls.name: Prompt instruction: escalate to a human only if the customer seems angry
controls.decay_rationale: Escalation depends entirely on the model's own judgment of affect; there is no structural gate requiring human review before send.

controls.name: SIEM logging of outbound email
controls.decay_rationale: Logging is enforced outside the model and does not decay with capability, but it is purely detective: it records the send after it has already left the organization.

controls.name: Recipient confirmation bound to the ticket's verified sender address
controls.decay_rationale: If the send recipient were taken from the system-of-record ticket rather than model output, the destination would be unreachable by attacker-supplied addresses under any model behavior.

controls.name: Scope CRM read to the authenticated requester's own record
controls.decay_rationale: A per-requester authorization check enforced at the CRM service, rather than a shared broad token, would make cross-customer reads unreachable regardless of model behavior.

controls.name: Raw-action human approval gate before external send containing customer data or a new recipient
controls.decay_rationale: A raw-action approval gate is enforced outside the model and does not decay with capability, though it can weaken under high approval volume (approval fatigue).

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): untrusted email drives a confidential CRM read and an external, irreversible email send

attack_path.note: Untrusted ticket content enters the agent's context.
Agent reads a confidential customer record using a broad, shared CRM credential.
Agent sends the record's contents externally using a shared mail credential, with no raw-action approval gate or destination binding.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: The model identifier/version in the environment variable changes with no corresponding review entry (subject.model.swappable is true), or either prompt instruction at prompt.md:5-6 or prompt.md:14 is edited or removed.

evidence.observation: Agent reads untrusted customer email and looks up CRM records; lookup is not restricted to the requester's own account.
Routine responses are sent directly without human review; escalation depends only on perceived anger.
mail_mcp uses a single static bearer token (MAIL_SVC_TOKEN) with no per-call approval or destination binding visible in the config.
MAIL_SVC_TOKEN is a shared service account that can send to any address; CRM_SVC_TOKEN can read every customer record.

recommendations.action: Add a raw-action human approval gate on cap.email_send for any message containing customer account data or addressed to a recipient not already on file for the ticket.
Bind the send recipient to the ticket's verified sender address from the system of record rather than letting the model choose or echo an address.
Scope the CRM credential to least privilege so reads are limited to the authenticated requester's own account absent an approved escalation.

findings.title: Confused deputy (ASI03): shared, broad CRM credential lets a request from any customer surface a different customer's confidential record

attack_path.note: Prompt explicitly permits lookup of any customer by email or account id, not only the requester's own record.
The retrieved (possibly third-party) record can be included in the outbound reply, with only a prompt instruction against cross-customer sharing.

forecast.watch_signal: The model is upgraded automatically with the platform with no review, or CRM_SVC_TOKEN's granted scope widens (new fields, endpoints, or record types added to crm_mcp).

evidence.observation: "You may look up any customer by email or account id" grants unrestricted CRM lookup regardless of who is emailing.
CRM_SVC_TOKEN can read every customer record, so the credential scope is broader than any single customer's own authority.
The only control against cross-customer disclosure is a prompt instruction, not a technical restriction on which records can be read or returned.

recommendations.action: Enforce at the CRM service (not the prompt) that a lookup must match the authenticated identity of the requesting ticket, absent an explicit escalation workflow.
Alert when a reply's CRM lookup key does not match the inbound sender's known account id or email.

findings.title: Destination control gap (ASI02): mail_send can address any external recipient with no binding to the ticket's verified sender

attack_path.note: Untrusted email content can specify or imply a reply destination the agent then uses.
mail_mcp.send uses a shared service token capable of addressing any external recipient, with no destination binding to the ticket's verified sender address.

findings.residual_rationale: ctl.never_share_other_customer and ctl.escalate_if_angry nominally cover cap.email_send, but neither one constrains recipient selection: one addresses content (not sharing another customer's data) and the other addresses timing (escalate if angry). Neither control reduces the chance that an untrusted email causes the reply to be misdirected to an attacker-controlled address, so no step-4 credit is given and residual stays at the inherent floor rather than the mechanical high.

forecast.watch_signal: No control currently constrains recipient selection, so this finding is already at its ceiling; watch for mail_mcp credential scope changes or any new egress tool (new_tool, new_mcp_server) that would open additional misdirection channels.

evidence.observation: mail_mcp.send is reachable with a shared service token; no recipient allowlist or binding is described in the config.
MAIL_SVC_TOKEN can send to any address.
The agent drafts and sends responses based on its own classification with no mention of verifying or constraining the recipient address.

recommendations.action: Bind the send recipient to the ticket's verified sender address from the system of record; never let the model supply or alter the destination.
Add a raw-action approval gate for any send to a recipient not already associated with the ticket.

rating.rationale: Every untrusted ticket can reach a confidential CRM read and an irreversible, shared-credential external send (U x S3 = critical on the base matrix). The only present controls are two prompt instructions (dependent, behavioral) and after-the-fact SIEM logging (detective only); there is no raw-action approval gate, no scoped CRM credential, and no recipient binding, so one finding's residual stays at the inherent ceiling by design judgment and the other two land at the mechanical floor of high. The model is upgraded with the platform with no separate review (subject.model.swappable: true), which is exactly the model_upgrade trigger that defeats both dependent prompt controls, pushing every finding back to critical under forecast. The single highest-leverage fix is a raw-action human approval gate combined with destination binding on cap.email_send, since neither currently exists and both are structural controls that do not decay with model capability.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in prompt.md, mcp.json, and the runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior.

No tool manifest or JSON schema for crm_mcp.get_customer or mail_mcp.send was provided; capability scoping and argument validation are inferred from the prompt and runtime notes, so confidence on exact exploitable fields is medium.
No agent card or explicit MCP authentication/handshake detail was provided, so peer_identity_verified and definitions_pinned are inferred as false/unknown rather than confirmed absent.
